qt: to the Commission Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left), Irene Montero (The Left) Subject:

Israel Aerospace Industries is an Israeli state-owned enterprise, a technology and arms production pillar of the Zionist State of Israel. In November, they published their profits, noting that the third quarter of 2024 has been the most profitable period in the company’s history. It participates in eight Horizon Europe projects, which have received over EUR 92 million in European Union funding. The Horizon Europe Annotated Grant Agreement says that the Commission may terminate the participation of a funding beneficiary if it commits criminal activities. Bearing in mind that, on the one hand, the company is state-owned and Israel is under investigation for genocide by the International Court of Justice, and that, on the other hand, there is an arrest warrant against Netanyahu for war crimes and crimes against humanity: 1.
Will the Commission withdraw funding from this company responsible for manufacturing the material used to carry out the occupation and genocide?

How does it justify having granted – and still granting – EU funding to a company controlled by a state that is under investigation for genocide and whose head of government has an arrest warrant issued against him for crimes against humanity?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.3.2025) Any research and innovation activities carried out under Horizon Europe1 must have an exclusive focus on civil applications. During the execution of project financed via Horizon Europe grant agreements, all beneficiaries must ensure that the activities under the action comply with this horizontal rule. The Commission is closely monitoring the correct implementation of grant agreements signed under Horizon Europe. The projects in which Israel Aerospace Industries participates are of a purely civil nature. These include, inter alia, projects to develop hybrid electric regional aircrafts, to revolutionise liquid hydrogen aircraft refuelling at airport scale, and to advance material science applications to reduce the generation of waste and enhance the safety of workers2. The Commission remains vigilant and is ready to take appropriate action should the Horizon Europe legal framework not be respected, notably regarding the exclusive focus on civil application as well as legally required behaviour of participants3. However, the actions or behaviour of the State of Israel cannot be considered automatically attributable to its entities participating in Horizon Europe grants.
